explanation: I searched Mathlib for any declaration stating this iterate result: greps for `frobeniusEquiv` combined with `^[n]` / `map_iterate` / `symm`, for `Semiconj`/`Commute` lemmas about frobenius (Algebra/CharP/Frobenius.lean, FieldTheory/Perfect.lean, RingTheory/Perfection.lean, RingTheory/WittVector/*, RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt.lean), and for generic iterate/Semiconj lemmas in Logic/Function/Iterate.lean and Logic/Function/Conjugate.lean. The only related Mathlib statements are (a) the one-step case `MonoidHom.map_frobeniusEquiv_symm` / `RingHom.map_frobeniusEquiv_symm` (line 237/242 of the same file, `n = 1`, a strictly different statement), (b) the generic combinatorics lemma `Function.Semiconj.iterate_right` (Logic/Function/Iterate.lean), and (c) the `frobenius` (not its inverse) version `MonoidHom.map_iterate_frobenius` / `RingHom.map_iterateFrobenius` in Algebra/CharP/Frobenius.lean. None of them states the iterate statement for `(frobeniusEquiv _ p).symm`: obtaining this theorem needs both the generic iterate lemma and the separate non-trivial fact that a monoid hom semiconjugates `(frobeniusEquiv R p).symm` to `(frobeniusEquiv S p).symm`, so it is not a single-declaration specialization under the stated criteria.
